parts.what: MATCH THIS SCREEN applies itself when the page opens
parts.seen: the page reported a 1280x800 screen; the browser decoded 1280x800 (the PC took the middle 2304x1440 of its 3440x1440 screen)
the PC answered 1280x720; the browser decoded 1280x720

parts.what: ask({shape:'match', viewWidth:1920, viewHeight:1200}) gives a 16:10 picture no taller than 1200
parts.seen: the PC answered 1728x1080 from the middle 2304x1440; the browser decoded 1728x1080

parts.what: ask({shape:'native', lines:'native'}) gives the whole 3440x1440 screen
parts.seen: the PC answered 3440x1440 (as it is); the browser decoded 3440x1440

parts.what: ask({fps:30}) brings the frames a second near 30
parts.seen: at 60 asked the browser decoded 57.0 frames a second; at 30 asked, 30.9 (the PC says it is sending up to 30)

parts.what: with a match running, native lines at 180 frames a second is answered with the cap
parts.seen: asked for native lines, 180 frames a second, 40 Mbit/s; the PC answered cap "LEAGUE MATCH", sending 2580x1080 at up to 60 frames a second, 12000 kbit/s; the browser decoded 2580x1080; the panel says "CAPPED BY THE PC: LEAGUE MATCH"

parts.what: the stream survives every change without reconnecting
parts.seen: one peer connection throughout, "connected" after every change (a: connected, b: connected, e: connected, c: connected, d: connected, h: connected). From the ask to the first decoded frame at the new size: (b) 400 ms, (c) 378 ms, (d) 390 ms

parts.what: the panel's own keys do what they say
parts.seen:
yes: [ SETTINGS ] opens the panel
      yes: the panel says what the PC is really sending
      yes: pressing [ 16:9 ] and [ 1080 ] changed the picture (decoded 1920x1080)
      yes: the [ 16:9 ] key shows as pressed
      yes: OFF shows the picture at its real size (1920x1080 drawn 1920x1080)
      yes: SHARP draws in hard squares (image-rendering: pixelated)
      yes: SMOOTH fills the window
      yes: SHARPENED draws a 1280x720 canvas, 38 frames so far, 97% of the sampled points lit, and on average 2.06 levels (of 255) away from the plain picture (most 52)
      yes: [ NUMBERS ] takes the corner readout away
      yes: and puts it back
      yes: the READOUT shows the stream
      yes: [ FULLSCREEN ] took the page fullscreen
      yes: the choices are remembered on this device ({"match":false,"shape":"16:9","lines":1080,"fps":60,"bitrateKbps":20000,"upscaling":"smooth","numbers":true})
      yes: Esc closes the panel

parts.what: on a new visit the remembered settings are sent to the PC again
parts.seen: after a reload the PC was asked for 16:9 at 1080 lines; the browser decoded 1920x1080

parts.what: a match starting mid-stream caps it, and what was asked for comes back when the match ends
parts.seen: before: 2560x1440 at 30000 kbit/s; match "started": 1920x1080 at 12000 kbit/s, cap "LEAGUE MATCH", seen by the page 2236 ms later; match "ended": 2560x1440 at 30000 kbit/s, seen 3010 ms later; connection connected, 1 made (the engine looks for the game once a second and the page reads the PC's settings every 3 s, so a few seconds is expected)
